rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has lawwāḥatun in the nominative as an adjective of Saqar in what is Saqar; it may also be an implied predicate, while ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī reads it accusatively as an adjective of Saqar in sa-uṣlīhi Saqar.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: لواحة بالرفع على أنه نعت للسقر في قوله: ما سقر

rows.speaker: عطية العوفي
rows.claim: ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī reads lawwāḥatan in the accusative, making it an adjective of Saqar in sa-uṣlīhi Saqar.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عطية العوفي: لواحة بالنصب على أنه نعت لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣlāʾ means consigning someone to the place of fire; its root sense is remaining or sticking there.
rows.anchor: الإصلاء: إلزام موضع النار، أصلاه يصليه إصلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is an indeclinable feminine proper name for Hell, named from the sun's painful scorching of the brain; the name reflects the fire's intense pain.
rows.anchor: سقر: اسم من أسماء جهنم، ولا ينصرف؛ لأنه مؤنث معرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related word saqr/sakr for a falcon uses the same root by analogy with the severity of its attack's pain.
rows.anchor: ومنه: السقر والصقر بالسين والصاد: الجارحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibqāʾ is leaving some of what was taken; abqāhu Allāh means that God prolong his life, and al-bāqī is what continues to exist.
rows.anchor: والإبقاء: ترك شيء مما أخذ، أبقى يبقي إبقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talwīḥ is changing color, as the sun changes a person's complexion; lawwāḥah intensifies the sense of repeated or extreme scorching.
rows.anchor: والتلويح: التغيير للون، لوحته الشمس تلوحه تلويحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basharah is the skin's outer surface, plural bashar; humans are called bashar because their skin is exposed rather than covered in fur or hair.
rows.anchor: والبشرة: ظاهر الجلدة، وجمعها: بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malak originally means messenger, then became specific to a class of accountable beings with a particular form; the cited poetry illustrates messenger and angel usage.
rows.anchor: والملك: أصله الرسالة إلا أنه اختص بنوع من المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form tisʿata ʿashara is accusative because two nouns have been joined to form one name.
rows.anchor: نصب (تسعة عشر) لأنهما اسمان جعلا اسما واحدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك
rows.claim: After hearing that Hell has nineteen keepers, Abū Jahl mocked Quraysh's numbers; Abū al-Asad offered to handle seventeen while they handled two, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى: (وما جعلنا أصحاب النار) الآية، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: A report from Muqātil says Abū Jahl claimed Muhammad had only nineteen helpers, prompting revelation that only God knows His hosts.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى: (وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو)، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the disbeliever, the passage follows with a threat against him: God will consign him to Saqar.
rows.anchor: ثم عقب ذكر الكافر بالوعيد له، فقال سبحانه: سأصليه سقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He will bring the disbeliever into the fire and keep him there perpetually.
rows.anchor: أي: سأدخله النار، وألزمه دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is variously described as one level of Hell, one of its gates, or one of its names.
rows.anchor: سقر: قيل: درك من دركات جهنم، وقيل: باب من أبوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses the listener and asks about Saqar's severity, essence, and measure.
rows.anchor: وما أدراك أيها السامع ما سقر: شدته وكنهه ومقداره

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim takes the phrase as the ultimate description of burning: Saqar burns everything.
rows.anchor: هو نهاية الوصف بالإحراق، أي: تحرق كل شيء، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says Saqar leaves none of its inhabitants alive or dead, but burns them again whenever they are recreated.
rows.anchor: ولا تذره ميتا، لكن تحرقهم كلما جدد خلقهم، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says Saqar reaches everyone in Hell and leaves no one without punishment.
rows.anchor: لا يبقى أحد من أهلها أن تتناوله، ولا تذره من العذاب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says Saqar burns everything and spares no one, exhausting its victims with every kind of punishment.
rows.anchor: ولا تذر أي: لا إبقاء عليهم؛ بل تبلغ مجهودهم في أنواع العذاب، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says Saqar leaves its victims with neither flesh nor bone.
rows.anchor: لا تبقي لهم لحما، ولا تذر لهم عظما، عن السدي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Saqar completely consumes people, then consumes them again after their return; unlike everything else, Hell never tires.
rows.anchor: وإذا أعيدوا لم تذرهم حتى تفنيهم، ولكل شيء فترة وملالة إلا لجهنم، عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar changes the skin's color, especially making the sufferers' complexions very dark.
rows.anchor: للجلود تلوح ألوانهم لا سيما إذا اشتد سوادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the tortured person's color changes when he sees Saqar.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إذا شاهدها المعذب تغير لونه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says one blast from Saqar scorches the skin and leaves it darker than night.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: تلفح الجلد لفحة فتدعه أشد سوادا من الليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Zayd ibn Aslam explain lawwāḥah as burning the skin.
rows.anchor: محرقة للجلود، عن ابن عباس، وزيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن، والأصم
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Aṣamm say Hellfire appears to its victims until they see it with their own eyes.
rows.anchor: تلوح لهم جهنم حتى يروها عيانا، عن الحسن، والأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed referents for the nineteen are classes, chiefs, or kinds; most commentators identify them as nineteen angels, with other helpers also present.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تسعة عشر جنسا، وقيل: تسعة عشر ملكا، وعليه أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors the majority view that the nineteen are angels, reasoning that if they suffice, there is no point in adding more.
rows.anchor: وعليه أكثر المفسرين، وإذا وقع الكفاية بهؤلاء فلا معنى لضم الزيادة إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the nineteen were specified to match what the Prophet reported from earlier prophets and what earlier scriptures said.
rows.anchor: ليوافق خبر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أخبار الأنبياء، وما كان في الكتب المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies these as the keepers of Saqar, while other gates and levels of the Fire have other keepers.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء خزان سقر، وللنار، ودركاتها الأخر خزان أخر

words: وَمَا جَعَلْنَآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَٰٓئِكَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions or keepers of the Fire whom God appointed are angels.
rows.anchor: أي: جعلنا الخزنة ملائكة

words: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةًۭ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers' number is a trial and test for disbelievers, who are challenged to believe it, and a test for the People of the Book concerning the Prophet's truthfulness.
rows.anchor: أي: شدة تعبد واختبار؛ لأنه كلفهم تصديقه، وامتحن أهل الكتاب ليعلموا صدقه

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the small number is a test to show that God can strengthen them so that they can do the work of a much larger number.
rows.anchor: ليعلموا أنه قادر على تقويتهم، وأنهم يقومون مقام العدد الكثير، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book, Jews and Christians, are to become certain the report is true because it agrees with their scriptures.
rows.anchor: من اليهود والنصارى أنه حق؛ لموافقة خبره لما في كتبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the number proves that God can give one being strength equal to that of many.
rows.anchor: ليعلموا أنه يقدر أن يجعل في واحد من القوة ما يقوم بخلق كثير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatādah, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk report that the number nineteen is stated in the Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي في التوراة والإنجيل: تسعة عشر، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that believers' faith is first made manifest, then grows stronger.
rows.anchor: ليظهر إيمانهم أيضا كما ظهر لغيره ليزدادوا إيمانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says believers grow in faith because the report conveys what only God could know, so they recognize it as a miracle and God's speech.
rows.anchor: لأنه يخبرهم بما لا يعلم إلا الله فيعلمون أنه معجز، وأنه كلام الله سبحانه

words: وَلَا يَرْتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book and believers should not doubt that the report is true, God's power, or the Prophet's prophethood.
rows.anchor: لا يشك الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون في أنه الحق، وفي قدرة الله

words: وَلِيَقُولَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌۭ وَٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes the lām as the lām of consequence: they hear it and say this while intending disbelief; another takes it as a prediction of what they will say.
rows.anchor: قيل: اللام لام العاقبة، يعني إذا سمعوا قالوا هذا، وغرضهم التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although one view takes those with sickness in their hearts as hypocrites, the author favors dissent and disbelief because the verse is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy there.
rows.anchor: الآية مكية وليس بها نفاق والكافرون ماذا أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the disbelievers ask what the count nineteen means and grow more doubtful.
rows.anchor: قيل: ببيان هذا العدد وما معنى تسعة عشر، يزدادون شكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they ask why nineteen should frighten them when they vastly outnumber that count, not realizing one angel could equal many.
rows.anchor: قالوا: ما معنى التخويف بتسعة عشر مع كثرة عددنا؟ وظنوا أن العدد شرط

words: كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as God made the angel keepers and their number a trial, He imposes duties that reveal who is astray and who is guided; misguidance is attributed to Him because the test originates in His command.
rows.anchor: كما جعلنا خزنة النار ملائكة ذوي عدد محنة واختبارا، كذلك يكلف ليظهر الضلال والهدى

words: كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim interprets this as God leading whom He wills away from Paradise and reward and guiding whom He wills to them, or destroying some and rewarding others.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يهلك من يشاء ويثيب من يشاء، عن أبي مسلم

words: كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says God rules that people are astray or guided according to what He finds in them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يحكم بضلال من يشاء، وبهداية من يشاء على حسبما يوجد منهم

words: كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As He consigns this disbeliever to Saqar, God likewise deals with whom He wills by leading astray or rewarding them.
rows.anchor: كما أصلى هذا الكافر سقر كذلك يفعل الله بمن يشاء أن يضله أو يثيبه

words: كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī takes kadhalika to mean that God punishes whom He wills and turns him away from Paradise, while guiding whom He wills to it.
rows.anchor: يعذب من يشاء ويصرفه عن الجنة، ويهدي إليه من يشاء، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as a person offering an excuse or stating his defense.
rows.anchor: قيل: لو اعتذر، أي: قال عذره، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says a person's testimony against himself is stronger than his false excuses.
rows.anchor: فشهادته على نفسه أولى من معاذيره الكاذبة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains al-maʿādhīr as making an excuse or arguing in one's own defense.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من اعتذاره، عن الفراء، أي: ولو اعتذر، وجادل عن نفسه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the phrase means that even if he presented an excuse to other people, it would not avail him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لو أقام الاعتذار عند الناس، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: السدي، والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk explain the phrase as lowering curtains and closing doors, which still cannot conceal a person.
rows.anchor: لو أرخى الستور وأغلق الأبواب، عن السدي، والضحاك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says that even if a person brought an excuse, it would not help him.
rows.anchor: لو أتى بعتبه لم ينفعه، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim takes al-maʿādhīr as people shifting blame onto one another, as in the cited confession that they obeyed their leaders.
rows.anchor: المعاذير إحالة بعضهم على بعض بالذنب، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ilqāʾ, literally casting or placing, means to say something.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الإلقاء: أن يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that no helper or supporter is available to the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على أنه لا معين ولا ظهير لأهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that no excuse will be accepted there.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه لا يقبل ثم عذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows they have no valid excuse, since a sound excuse would have been accepted.
rows.anchor: وتدل أنه لا عذر لهم؛ إذ لو كان عذر صحيح لقبل منهم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو، وابن عامر، ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Yaʿqūb read the following verbs yuḥibbūna and yadharūna in the third person; the others read them in the second person.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ويعقوب: يحبون، ويذرون بالياء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥrīk is causing something to move from one direction to another; motion is a state that follows its contrary, and in the author's account motion and rest belong to the genus of spatial states.
rows.anchor: التحريك: التصيير من جهة إلى أخرى بالحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjalah means doing something before its proper time, opposite to delay.
rows.anchor: والعجلة: عمل الشيء قبل وقته الذي ينبغي فيه، ونقيضه: الإبطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following, emulating, and imitating are near-synonyms; following means the second thing conforms to the first, opposite to differing from it.
rows.anchor: والاتباع والاقتداء والاحتذاء نظائر، والاتباع: موافقة الثاني للأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayān is making a meaning apparent to the mind in a way that distinguishes it from other meanings.
rows.anchor: والبيان: إظهار المعنى للنفس بما يتبين به من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾān derives from gathering and joining and is a verbal noun like rujḥān and nuqṣān; qaraʾtu water in a basin means I gathered it.
rows.anchor: والقرآن: أصله من الضم والجمع، وهو مصدر كالرجحان والنقصان

rows.speaker: مجاهد، وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatādah report that the Prophet frequently moved his tongue with the Qurʾān for fear of forgetting it, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فنزل: (لا تحرك به لسانك)، عن مجاهد، وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk report that the Prophet hurriedly moved his tongue when revelation came because he loved it; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان إذا نزل القرآن عجل بتحريك لسانه لحبه إياه، فنزل: (لا تحرك)، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is also linked to the instruction not to hasten with the Qurʾān before its revelation is completed.
rows.anchor: وفيه نزل: (ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One coherence reading takes this as an address to the Prophet in worldly life: after the warning of resurrection, he should recite slowly and repeat so the message settles in people's hearts; God's proofs will be clarified, while people need repeated reminders because worldly love distracts them from the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: أن هذا خطاب للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في الدنيا، ونظم الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the worldly-life reading, the Prophet should not rush the recitation but repeat and recite in measured fashion so it becomes established in their hearts.
rows.anchor: بل كررها عليهم، ورتل ليتقرر في قلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the address as directed to disbelievers at the resurrection, as they hastily read their record of deeds in distress.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الخطاب للكفار يوم القيامة، فلما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this alternative, they are told not to hurry through their record but to read carefully, since it gathers evidence against them and they must submit to its judgment.
rows.anchor: فإنا نجمعها لك، فإذا جمعناه فاتبع ما جمع عليك بالانقياد لحكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection address fits the preceding mention of what a person has sent ahead and left behind better, but the worldly address is closer to the apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه أليق بما قدم وأخر، غير أن الأول أقرب إلى الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another connection links love of the present life to the preceding statement that a person wants to sin ahead: love of worldly pleasures leads him to choose them over the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قوله: (تحبون العاجلة) يتصل بقوله: (بل يريد الإنسان ليفجر أمامه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here bih means the Qurʾān or revelation; the Prophet moved his tongue to hasten its memorization and avoid forgetting it.
rows.anchor: لا تحرك به لسانك يعني بالقرآن والوحي لتعجل به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk explain God's gathering it as placing the Qurʾān in the Prophet's chest until he memorizes it, and its recitation as enabling him to repeat and explain it.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن علينا جمعه في صدرك حتى تحفظه، وقرآنه عليك حتى تعيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah explains gathering as collecting the Qurʾān in the Prophet's chest and arranging it in the order revealed to him.
rows.anchor: إن علينا جمعه في صدرك، وتأليفه على ما نزل عليك، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the promise as God's preserving the Qurʾān for the Prophet so he can recite it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: علينا حفظه عليك لتصل إلى الأداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aim is not merely recitation and memorization but reflection on the Qurʾān and knowledge of its meanings and rulings; preservation is God's responsibility, so the Prophet should attend to his own duty.
rows.anchor: فأشار إلى أن المقصود ليس مجرد التلاوة والحفظ؛ بل التدبر فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains following its recitation as reciting it oneself after hearing it.
rows.anchor: أي: اتبع قرآنه بقراءتك، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة، والضحاك
rows.claim: Qatādah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk interpret following its recitation as acting on the Qurʾān's rulings.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فاعمل بما فيه من الأحكام، عن قتادة، والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is to act on the Qurʾān and convey it to the Prophet's community.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اعمل به وبلغه أمتك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the promise of clarification as God reminding the Prophet of the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: نذكره لك، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah explains the clarification as stating the Qurʾān's rulings and what is lawful and forbidden.
rows.anchor: نذكر أحكامه وحلاله وحرامه، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God will explain the Qurʾān's meaning, its rulings, and its clear and ambiguous passages after the Prophet memorizes it.
rows.anchor: نبين لك معناه إذا حفظته، وبيان أحكامه، ومحكمه، ومتشابهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā is a rebuke and deterrent against loving worldly life and following desire.
rows.anchor: كلا ردع وزجر عن حب الدنيا واتباع الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, kallā means truly: they fail to reflect because they love immediate life and leave the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه حقا، كأنه قيل: لا يتدبرون؛ لأنهم يحبون العاجلة ويذرون الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They choose worldly life over the afterlife and work for this world rather than the next out of ignorance and poor judgment; the passage expresses wonder at their choice.
rows.anchor: يختارون الدنيا على العقبى، فيعملون للدنيا لا للآخرة جهلا منهم وسوء اختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes a miracle: revelation was fixed in the Prophet's chest without study, contrary to ordinary experience.
rows.anchor: يدل قوله: (لا تحرك) الآية، على معجزة، حيث يثبت الوحي في صدره من غير درس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ʿalaynā signals obligation because ʿalā is a word of obligation; once commissioned, the Prophet was obliged to explain what removes the accountable person's excuse.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (إن علينا جمعه) أنه يجب عليه شيء؛ لأن (على) كلمة إيجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that choosing the afterlife over the immediate world is obligatory; those who choose the perishing world over lasting, pure reward are blameworthy.
rows.anchor: قوله: (تحبون العاجلة) على أن الواجب اختيار الآخرة على الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that existence alone makes God visible: many existing things cannot be seen, and extending the premise to other senses would make God touchable, smellable, or tasteable.
rows.anchor: لا نسلم؛ لأن كثيرا من الموجودات لا ترى

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim pronounces the nūn in min rāqin distinctly, with a brief pause; the other readers assimilate it, as they do in bal rāna.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم: من راق بإظهار النون يقف عليه وقفة يسيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-tarāqī are the paired bones around the throat; another description calls them the upper front of the throat, where the soul rises and death rattles occur.
rows.anchor: التراقي: العظام المكتنفة للحلق يمينا وشمالا، وقيل: مقدم الحلق

rows.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
rows.claim: The cited line by Durayd ibn al-Ṣimmah uses al-tarāqī for the place the soul reaches at death.
rows.anchor: فرب عظيمة دافعت عنهم ... وقد بلغت نفوسهم التراقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rāqī is someone seeking a cure; ruqyah seeks healing through God's names and Qurʾānic verses, while an ʿawdhah wards off calamity through God's words.
rows.anchor: والراقي: الطالب للشفاء، رقاه يرقيه رقية: إذا طلب له الشفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs often turned to healers, and the cited poem speaks of people trying every healing incantation and soothing remedy.
rows.anchor: وكانت العرب تفزع إلى الرقاة كثيرا، ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs use ساق to express the severity of a matter, as in the idiom that war stands on a ساق and the cited poetic usage.
rows.anchor: العرب تذكر الساق، وتريد شدة الأمر، يقولون: قامت الحرب على ساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-masāq means the place to which a person is driven and derives from the verb for driving.
rows.anchor: والمساق: الموضع الذي يساق إليه، وأصله من السوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawallī means turning away.
rows.anchor: والتولي: الإعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamattī means stretching one's belly from laziness; it comes from madd, and the form yamattaṭu changed one emphatic tāʾ into yāʾ.
rows.anchor: والتمطي: تمدد البطن عن الكسل، والمط: المد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another etymology derives the word from yalwī maṭāhu, twisting his back, with maṭā meaning the back.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أصله: يلوى مطاه، والمطا: الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation takes awlā from walī, nearness, as in the command to fight those who are nearest to you.
rows.anchor: قيل: أصله الولي، وهو القرب، ومنه: (قاتلوا الذين يلونكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says awlā in an action means more entitled to it, and it also carries the sense of nearness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأولى في الفعل هو الأحق، وهو أيضا من القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says the verses concern Abū Jahl, who was killed at Badr in a terrible manner; a Prophetic report calls Abū Jahl the Pharaoh of this community.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآيات في أبي جهل، وقتل يوم بدر شر مقتل، عن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the Prophet met Abū Jahl outside the mosque and said awlā laka fa-awlā; Abū Jahl boasted that neither Muhammad nor his Lord could harm him, then went inside shaken, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فاستقبله أبو جهل، فقال - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: (أولى لك فأولى) فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā may mean truly, or deny what they think and warn that they will learn the truth when the soul reaches the collarbones.
rows.anchor: قيل: حقا، وقيل: ليس الأمر كما يظنون، ولكن سيعلمون إذا بلغت التراقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul reaching the collarbones is expressed by ellipsis: the soul is not named, but the context indicates it.
rows.anchor: بلغت النفس التراقي كناية عن غير مذكور؛ لأن في الكلام ما يدل عليه

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة، والضحاك، وقتادة، وابن زيد
rows.claim: Abū Qilābah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Qatādah, and Ibn Zayd say those present ask whether a healer can perform ruqyah and treat the dying person.
rows.anchor: من حضره: هل من راق؛ أي: من طبيب يرقيه ويداويه، عن أبي قلابة، والضحاك، وقتادة، وابن زيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah says the people sought physicians, but they could not avert God's decree.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: التمسوا له الأطباء، فلم يغنوا عنه من قضاء الله شيئا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وأبو الحوراء، ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-Ḥawrāʾ, and Muqātil say the angels ask which group will take the soul up, the angels of mercy or of punishment.
rows.anchor: قالت الملائكة من يرقى بروحه أملائكة الرحمة أم ملائكة العذاب؟ عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliyah says the angels of mercy and punishment dispute over which of them will take the soul up.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية: تختصم فيه ملائكة الرحمة وملائكة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anticipated separation is from worldly life, family, property, and children.
rows.anchor: أي: فراق الدنيا والأهل والمال والولد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that a dying servant endures the pangs of death as his joints bid each other farewell, knowing they will part until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: إن العبد ليعالج كرب الموت وسكراته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view places this at the moment of seeing death and takes ẓann to mean certain knowledge; another places it earlier, when he still hopes to recover but expects separation.
rows.anchor: والظن بمعنى العلم، وقيل: هو قبله حتى يرجو الصحة، ويظن الفراق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والحسن، والربيع
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, and al-Rabīʿ explain the phrase as the severity of the affairs of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: قيل: شدة أمر الدنيا وأمر الآخرة، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والحسن، والربيع

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the people of this world prepare the body while the people of the next prepare the soul.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أهل الدنيا يجهزون البدن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan offers an interpretation involving the state of death and the state of life coming together.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حال الموت بحال الحياة، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الشعبي، وأبو مالك
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and Abū Mālik say the person's legs stiffen at death as strength leaves them and they become like folded skin.
rows.anchor: ويبسهما عند الموت، عن الشعبي، وأبي مالك؛ لأنه تذهب القوة

rows.speaker: الحسن، وسعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Another report, attributed to al-Ḥasan with disagreement and to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, says the legs are wrapped in the shroud.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التفاف الساقين في الكفن، عن الحسن بخلاف، وسعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the leg of worldly life joins that of the afterlife, meaning the agony of death and terror of what follows.
rows.anchor: ساق الدنيا بساق الآخرة، وهو شدة كرب الموت، وشدة هول المطلع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah describes the dying person as struggling, stretching one leg while letting the other fall and wrapping one around the other.
rows.anchor: يضطرب فلا يزال يمد إحدى رجليه، ويرسل الأخرى، ويلف إحداهما بالأخرى، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan also says the legs cease to carry the person who used to walk on them.
rows.anchor: ماتت رجلاه، فلم تحملاه وكان عليهما جوالا، عن الحسن أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations describe the grief of leaving family and the world and facing God without knowing what awaits, the loss of all one's possessions and questioning about them, or the final worldly day joining the first day of the next life.
rows.anchor: يلتف عليه غم فراق الدنيا والأهل، وغم القدوم على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says successive hardships surround the dying person: death throes, impending death, leaving the world, and the grief of the grave.
rows.anchor: وغم القبر، ونحو ذلك، عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the dying person cannot leave one distress before a more severe one comes.
rows.anchor: لا يخرج من كربة إلا جاءه أشد منها، عن السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is driven to God's judgment and whatever He decrees for him; this urges obedience and warns against disobedience.
rows.anchor: يعني يساق إلى حكمه، وما يأمر له فيه، وذلك حث على طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says an angel drives the soul to the destination God commands.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يسوق الملك روحه إلى حيث أمر الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbeliever is also addressed by the obligations of prayer and almsgiving.
rows.anchor: ومنها: أن الكافر مخاطب بهما

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: Abū Hāshim holds that punishment may be deserved for failing to perform an obligation; Abū ʿAlī disagrees.
rows.anchor: على ما يقوله شيخنا أبو هاشم: أن العقاب قد يستحق على ألا يفعل الواجب

rows.speaker: الحسن، وأبو عمرو، وحفص عن عاصم، ويعقوب
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqūb read yumnā with yāʾ, following al-manī; the rest read it with tāʾ, following al-nuṭfah, as Abū Ḥātim prefers, while Abū ʿUbayd prefers yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب: يمنى بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sudā means left unattended without being held accountable; the related expression for camels means grazing wherever they please.
rows.anchor: السدى: المهمل، وهو أن يهمل من غير أن يؤخذ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfah is the male reproductive fluid from which a person is created; the word originally means a small amount of water, though it can also refer to more.
rows.anchor: والمني: هو النطفة، الماء الذي يخلق منه الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlaqah is a piece of congealed blood.
rows.anchor: والعلقة: القطعة من الدم المنعقد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Readers pronounce the phrase with clear articulation; al-Farrāʾ permits assimilation by moving the vowel to the ḥāʾ and cites a line for the form.
rows.anchor: القراء (على أن يحيي الموتى) بالإظهار، وأجاز الفراء بالإدغام

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib reports that when the verse asking whether God can resurrect the dead was revealed, the Prophet said, Glorified are You, indeed You can.
rows.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب: لما نزلت هذه الآية: (أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse explains that people are not left without purpose or accountability; its initial hamzah is an interrogative used here to deny and rebuke the thought.
rows.anchor: ثم بين تعالى أنهم لم يتركوا هملا زجرا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial alif is an interrogative, with the force of disapproval.
rows.anchor: الألف ألف استفهام، والمراد الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān means humankind generally, which the author says is the stronger view; Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identify the referent as Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: الإنسان، قيل: أراد الجنس وهو الوجه. وقيل: أراد أبا جهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid take the claim of being left suda as being left neglected, with no commands or prohibitions.
rows.anchor: أن يترك سدى مهملا، لا يؤمر ولا ينهى، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who sees his changing stages of creation should know he has a wise maker; after granting maturity, reason, ability, and desire, God would not leave him without religious duties.
rows.anchor: وهو يرى في نفسه من تنقل الأحوال ما يدل أن له صانعا حكيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yumnā may mean measured or determined, or emitted from the male sexual organ.
rows.anchor: يمنى قيل: يقدر، وقيل: يخرج من ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The semen becomes a clot; God then creates and forms the person, including internal and external organs, in the womb.
rows.anchor: صار المني علقة فخلق، ثم خلق منه الخلق فسوى خلقه وصوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says God proportioned the clot into a human being as people observe.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سواه إنسانا على ما نشاهده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pair of male and female may be created from the human being, or from the semen; either account points to a purpose, exposure to reward through religious obligation.
rows.anchor: قيل: من الإنسان من الذكر والأنثى وقيل: من المني، فلا بد من غرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who created human beings in these stages can resurrect the dead for judgment and recompense.
rows.anchor: من جعل ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى للبعث والجزاء

words: وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ ءَاثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا
rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The qāḍī says Sūrat al-Insān is Meccan, though this is disputed; most say it is entirely Meccan, while others say the whole sūra is Medinan.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي: وهي مكية على اختلاف فيه، وقيل: كلها مكية

words: وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ ءَاثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا
rows.speaker: مجاهد، وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatādah are cited for the view that the whole sūra is Medinan.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كلها مدنية، عن مجاهد، وقتادة

words: وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ ءَاثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا
rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrimah say the verse prohibiting obedience to a sinner or disbeliever is Meccan and the rest of the sūra is Medinan.
rows.anchor: وهي قوله: (ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا) والباقي مدنية، عن الحسن وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra contains thirty-one verses.
rows.anchor: وهي إحدى وثلاثون آية

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب، النبي
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb transmits from the Prophet that whoever recites Sūrat Hal Atā will receive Paradise and silk as a reward from God.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (هل أتى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Insān begins by repeating the proof from human creation that closed Sūrat al-Qiyāmah, which had ended by affirming resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (لا أقسم) بصحة البعث، وما دل عليه من خلق الإنسان من نطفة، ابتدأ هذه السورة بمثل ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read salāsilan with tanwīn in connected recitation and an alif when stopping, to match the surrounding verse endings.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع والكسائي، وأبو بكر عن عاصم: سلاسلا بالتنوين في الوصل

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وحمزة ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamzah, and Yaʿqūb read salāsil without tanwīn and stop without an alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحمزة ويعقوب: سلاسل بغير تنوين والوقف بغير ألف

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read without tanwīn in connected recitation but stop with an alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم: سلاسل بغير تنوين في الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with tanwīn is chosen to match the nearby verse endings.
rows.anchor: فمن نون فلتشاكل ما جاوره من رؤوس الآي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hal is an interrogative particle, also used with the meaning qad.
rows.anchor: هل: حرف استفهام، يقال: هل رأيت زيدا؟ واستعمل بمعنى (قد)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān is an animal of the familiar human form who moves, eats, and drinks and lives by an animating life; the author says this is the strongest definition.
rows.anchor: الإنسان: حيوان على الصورة المعروفة، وهي هذا القالب الذاهب الجائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dahr is the passage of night and day, with plurals adhur and duhūr.
rows.anchor: والدهر: مرور الليل والنهار، وجمعه: أدهر، ودهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfah is man's fluid; originally it means a small amount of water in a container, though it can also refer to more, and its plurals include niṭāf and nuṭaf.
rows.anchor: والنطفة: ماء الرجل، وأصله: الماء القليل يكون في إناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amshāj means mixtures, its singular is mashj, and the verb mashaǧtu means I mixed one thing with another.
rows.anchor: والأمشاج: الأخلاط، واحدها: مشج، ومشجت هذا بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtalāʾ means testing or choosing; since God cannot literally be tested, He treats people as a tester would so what He already knows becomes manifest.
rows.anchor: والابتلاء: الاختيار، وحقيقته لا تجوز عليه تعالى، وإنما يعامل معاملة المختبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat ʿAbasa is Meccan and contains forty-five verses.
rows.anchor: مكية، خمس وأربعون آية

rows.speaker: أبي، النبي
rows.claim: Ubayy transmits from the Prophet that whoever recites Sūrat ʿAbasa wa-Tawallā will come on the Day of Resurrection with a smiling, delighted face.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (عبس وتولى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the previous sūra ends by calling the Prophet a warner for whoever fears the Resurrection, this sūra opens by mentioning his turning from one who does not fear it and attending to people whose conversion he hopes for, as instruction for the community.
rows.anchor: ولما ختم السورة بقوله: (إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها) افتتح هذه السورة بذكر إعراضه

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads fatanfaʿahu with fatḥah on the ʿayn as a subjunctive result after laʿalla and fa; the others read it with ḍammah, coordinated with yuzakkā and yadhdhakkaru.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم: فتنفعه بنصب. العين على جواب (لعل) بالفاء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, and Ibn Kathīr read taṣaddā with a doubled ṣād through assimilation from tataṣaddā; the other readers have a light ṣād after dropping the second tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير: تصدى بتشديد الصاد على الإدغام، وأصله تتصدى

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr assimilates the tāʾ into the lām in talahhā, whose original form is tatallahhā; the others read the lighter form with the extra tāʾ omitted.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: تلهى بإدغام التاء في اللام، وأصله: (تتلهى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbasa means contracting the face in displeasure and is synonymous with basara and taqṭīb; the name ʿAbbās derives from the same word.
rows.anchor: يقال: عبس فلان في وجه فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawallī means turning away.
rows.anchor: والتولي: الإعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yazzakkā derives from yatazakkā by assimilating tāʾ into zāy; yadhdhakkaru similarly derives from yatadhakkaru, while tazkiyah means purification and tadhakkur seeking a reminder.
rows.anchor: يزكى: أصله يتزكى فأدغمت التاء في الزاي، كما أدغمت في (يذكر)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣaddī means exposing oneself to something as a thirsty person approaches water; ṣadā is thirst, and the word also means to look expectantly toward something.
rows.anchor: والتصدي: التعرض للشيء كتعرض العطشان للماء، وأصل الصدى العطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ṣadā, echo, is explained either by dryness like a thirsty throat or by the echo's seeming to present speech by returning something like it.
rows.anchor: وسمي الصدى؛ لأنه بالجفاف صار كجفاف حلق العطشان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talahhī from something means turning away from it; talahhī with something means attending to it, and the verb can mean being distracted or heedless.
rows.anchor: والتلهي عن الشيء: الإعراض عنه، والتلهي به: الإقبال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root is also used in the verse saying rivalry for more has distracted you.
rows.anchor: ومنه: (ألهاكم التكاثر)
